properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 29 at 1:43PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 142 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Victor, or 16 miles west of Colorado Springs, moving northeast at 5
mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph, half inch hail and torrential
rainfall.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible. Heavy rainfall could cause ponding of water on
paved road surfaces, minor washouts on dirt roads, and
quick runoff causing high flows in area creeks, streams and
normally dry washouts.

Locations impacted include...
Cripple Creek, Victor, and Pikes Peak.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 1:29PM MDT until July 29 at 4:30PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Fremont County in central Colorado...

* Until 430 PM MDT.

* At 129 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2.5 inches of rain
have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour.
Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, roads, and
normally dry washes, as well as other poor drainage and
low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of North Central Fremont County along the
Cottonwood Creek drainage and its tributaries.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 29 at 1:02PM MDT until July 29 at 4:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Clear Creek County in central Colorado...
Southeastern Gilpin County in central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 400 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 102 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen.

- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Soda Creek, Ralston Creek, Lake Fork, Clear Creek, North Clear
Creek, Beaverdam Creek, Little Bear Creek, Chicago Creek, Silver
Creek, Barbour Fork, Fall River, Vance Creek, Missouri Creek and
South Chicago Creek. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches
are expected over the area. This additional rain will result in
minor flooding.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Idaho Springs, Central City, Black Hawk, Aspen Springs and
Russell Gulch.
